title: Present Middle and Passive
description: The present middle and passive of λύω, ὑπό with the genitive of the agent, the dative of means, deponent verbs, compound verbs and the place of οὐ.

blocks.caption: Summary
blocks.html: Greek has three voices. The active and passive are used as in English. The middle shows the subject acting on or for itself; in many verbs its sense cannot be shown in English. In the present the middle and passive have the same forms; in this unit's exercises read them as passive. A deponent verb (ἔρχομαι, γίνομαι, πορεύομαι, ἀποκρίνομαι) has middle or passive forms with an active meaning.

blocks.caption: λύομαι, I am being loosed
rows: The primary middle endings are -μαι, -σαι, -ται, -μεθα, -σθε, -νται, joined to the stem by the variable vowel ο (before μ and ν) or ε. In the second singular λύεσαι has become λύῃ.

blocks.caption: Agent and means
blocks.html: The personal agent of a passive verb is ὑπό with the genitive: λύεται ὑπὸ τοῦ κυρίου, he is loosed by the Lord. The thing by means of which something is done is the plain dative: ἐγείρονται τῷ λόγῳ τοῦ κυρίου, they are raised by the word of the Lord.

blocks.caption: Compound verbs and οὐ
blocks.html: A preposition prefixed to a verb often adds its own meaning: ἐκ + ἔρχομαι = ἐξέρχομαι, I go out; εἰς + ἔρχομαι = εἰσέρχομαι, I go in. οὐ stands before the word it negates, normally right before the verb; it is οὐκ before a smooth breathing and οὐχ before a rough one.

blocks.caption: Cases with verbs
blocks.html: ἀκούω may take the genitive (ἀκούω τῆς φωνῆς, I hear the voice) or the accusative; ἀποκρίνομαι takes the dative (ἀποκρίνομαι τῷ ἀποστόλῳ, I answer the apostle); ἄρχω, I rule, takes the genitive.
